facts.raw_span: A 61-year-old man presented with gross hematuria
Intravenous urography demonstrated a tubular filling defect with partial obstruction of the right mid ureter
Retrograde ureteropyelography confirmed a 5 cm long tubular mass in the mid ureter proximal to the iliac vessels
Urine cytology and endoscopic biopsy of the lesion and renal pelvis were negative for malignancy
A staging CT scan showed slight dilatation of the right renal pelvis and subtle thickening of the right ureter without evidence of metastasis or lymphadenopathy

concepts.why: The patient's presentation with gross hematuria and intermittent right pelvic pain, combined with imaging findings of a tubular filling defect and a 5 cm long tubular mass in the mid ureter, is consistent with a ureteral fibroepithelial polyp, which is a benign tumor that can cause obstructive symptoms and hematuria.

The patient's imaging findings, including a tubular filling defect and a 5 cm long tubular mass in the mid ureter, could also be consistent with a ureteral leiomyoma, which is a rare, benign tumor that can cause obstructive symptoms and hematuria.

The patient's presentation with gross hematuria and intermittent right pelvic pain, combined with imaging findings of a tubular filling defect and a 5 cm long tubular mass in the mid ureter, could also be consistent with a ureteral hemangioma, which is a rare, benign tumor that can cause obstructive symptoms and hematuria.
